study_name.evidence_quote: The study protocol was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT02217384 )
study_name.notes: Derived from registration number and publication year; no explicit study name provided

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.

country.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

location.evidence_quote: Center for Eating Disorders (Odense University Hospital), Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Unit (Aarhus University Hospital) and Unit for Psychiatric Research (Aalborg University Hospital)

body_site.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction
dna_extraction_kit.notes: For mouse studies: 'Microbial DNAs were isolated and purified from stool samples (~250 mg) of human donors and mouse recipients by using NucleoSpin soil mini kit (MACHEREY‑NAGEL)'

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher)
sequencing_platform.notes: Human samples sequenced on Ion Proton; mouse samples on Illumina MiSeq

sex.evidence_quote: Since 90–95% of individuals with diagnosed AN are females, we decided to include only women in the present study
sex.notes: Only female participants included for human cohort

ancestry.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

age_unit.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from randomly selected subsets of three patients with AN (females aged 20, 22 and 20 yr
age_unit.notes: Age reported in years for both human and mouse study donor information

westernized.evidence_quote: recruited via public advertisement and via direct contact to health staff, medical students and their relatives
westernized.notes: Danish Caucasian cohort from specialized medical centers indicates westernized population

age_min.evidence_quote: EDI-3 developed from current theories related to pathogenesis and diagnosis of eating disorders and it was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_min.notes: EDI-3 questionnaire was administered to all participants; age range provided for the assessment tool indicates the eligible age span for participants in this study.

age_max.evidence_quote: EDI-3 developed from current theories related to pathogenesis and diagnosis of eating disorders and it was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_max.notes: EDI-3 questionnaire was administered to all participants; age range provided for the assessment tool indicates the eligible age span for participants in this study.

bmi.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from randomly selected subsets of three patients with AN (females aged 20, 22 and 20 yr with BMI of 10.3, 11.5 and 11.7 kg m −2, respectively) and three HC (females aged 20, 22 and 21 yr with BMI of 22.6, 21.1 and 21.2 kg m −2, respectively)
bmi.notes: Study reports BMI values for the three AN donors (10.3, 11.5, 11.7) and three HC donors (22.6, 21.1, 21.2) used in FMT animal experiments. Exclusion criteria for HC specified BMI below 18.5 or above 25 kg/m². An cases had BMI consistent with eating disorder diagnosis.

disease.evidence_quote: The AN patients were all diagnosed by an experienced consultant psychiatrist and they met the DSM-5 criteria for the restricting or binge/purging subtypes of AN.
disease.notes: All AN participants met DSM-5 criteria for anorexia nervosa. HC participants had no eating disorders or other acute/chronic somatic diseases.

disease_details.evidence_quote: It can be classified into two subtypes, the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: Study included both AN-RS (n=56) and AN-BP (n=21) subtypes; AN-BP is described as less prevalent.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion applied to AN cases; participants with antibiotics/antifungal use within 3 months were excluded, ensuring no current use in enrolled participants.

smoker.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria for the age-matched healthy control women were BMI below 18.5 or above 25 kg m 21 −2 , regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills, and antibiotics within the last 3 months.
smoker.notes: Smoking status was used as a covariate in statistical analyses, indicating some participants were smokers, but specific prevalence is not reported in the main text or figures.

treatment.evidence_quote: multiple medications (selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics and benzodiazepines, specified in Supplementary Table 2)
treatment.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN
treatment.notes: Medications listed as covariates in statistical analyses; specific dosages and prevalence by group not reported in main text.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria for the age-matched healthy control women were BMI below 18.5 or above 25 kg m 21 −2 , regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Birth control pills were permitted in HC; use may have been present in both AN and HC groups.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: we transplanted faecal microbiota from three randomly chosen AN-RS cases and three age-matched HC participants to three independent litters of female germ-free (GF) mice
fmt_role.section: Results — Gut microbiota induces reduced weight gain and altered energy metabolism in mice
fmt_role.notes: Three AN-RS donors and three HC donors provided fecal material for FMT to GF mice; mice served as recipients after FMT procedure.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: No birth weight information reported for human participants.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: No gestational age information reported for human participants.

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: No delivery method information reported for human participants.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: No infant feeding method information reported for human participants.

zigosity.notes: No zygosity information reported for human participants; study used littermates in animal experiments but not twin studies in humans.

age_years.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from randomly selected subsets of three patients with AN (females aged 20, 22 and 20 yr with BMI of 10.3, 11.5 and 11.7 kg m −2, respectively) and three HC (females aged 20, 22 and 21 yr with BMI of 22.6, 21.1 and 21.2 kg m −2, respectively)
age_years.notes: Age reported only for the six donors (3 AN-RS, 3 HC) used in FMT experiments; study enrolled 77 AN and 70 HC but only described as age-matched without reporting the full distribution.

dietary_restriction.evidence_quote: reduced food intake, loss of body weight, raised physical activity and emotional rigidity
dietary_restriction.notes: Paper notes that AN is characterized by reduced food intake as a defining symptom, but specific dietary restriction details (e.g., calorie targets, specific foods avoided) are not systematically reported for human participants. The paper documents macronutrient composition (40–50% carbohydrate, 30–40% fat, 20–25% protein) for meals given to inpatients.

feces_phenotype.notes: Paper characterizes fecal microbiota composition and metabolites but does not report stool-related phenotypes (e.g., consistency, frequency) for participants.

disease_response_orr.notes: Study is not a treatment/intervention trial; ORR not applicable.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Study is observational and mechanistic; PFS not applicable.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Study is observational and mechanistic; PFS follow-up not applicable.

disease_response_recist.notes: Study is not an oncology trial; RECIST criteria not applicable.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Study does not involve cancer; AJCC staging not applicable.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: Study does not involve cancer; TNM staging not applicable.

obgyn_lactating.notes: No information on current lactation status provided.

obgyn_menopause.notes: No menopausal status information reported; participants were enrolled from specialized eating disorder centers (likely younger cohort) but exact age distribution for full cohort (n=147) not given.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: No pregnancy status information reported for enrolled participants.

fmt_id.notes: Study does not assign explicit FMT participant IDs; FMT donors and recipients are identified only by group (AN-T, HC-T) and litter (1, 2, 3) in figures.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: women with AN were much leaner, had lower fasting serum concentrations of glucose and insulin, higher insulin sensitivity
biomarker_name.section: Results — Phenotypes of women with AN and controls
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified from different sections of the paper related to metabolites, bacterial taxa, and clinical parameters

biomarker_unit.notes: Paper does not report specific units for most biomarkers in the text; units are implied but not explicitly stated for metabolites

value: positively correlated with eating disorder scores
inversely correlated with eating disorder scores
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: serum concentrations of indole-3-acetic acid and indole-3-propionic acid were higher in AN compared with HC
biomarker_value.section: Results — Serum metabolites are associated with markers of appetite and food intake regulation
biomarker_value.notes: Specific numerical values not provided for most biomarkers; qualitative comparisons (higher/lower/depleted/enriched) documented instead

disease_response_os.notes: This paper is observational/mechanistic and does not report overall survival data

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; paper does not report survival outcomes

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not reported in this anorexia nervosa mechanistic study

value: increased hypothalamic gene expression (Bdnf, Cartpt, Htr1b)
increased adipose tissue thermogenesis (Ucp1, Elovl3, Pgc1α)
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: AN microbiota samples were characterized by a reduction in Bacteroidota and Actinobacteriota
feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes include compositional and functional changes documented in both human and mouse studies

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this is a microbiota and metabolomics study of anorexia nervosa, not oncology

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; paper does not address tumor or residual disease

value: Cohort: 77 females with AN, 70 healthy female controls
Study location: Denmark (three specialized eating disorder centers)
AN subtypes: AN-RS (restricting, n=56) and AN-BP (binge-eating/purging, n=21)
Study population: Danish Caucasian women only
Patient setting: Both inpatients (n=35) and outpatients (n=42)
Animal model: Female germ-free Swiss Webster mice
FMT donors: 3 AN-RS cases and 3 healthy controls
FMT intervention: 30% energy-restricted diet for 3 weeks in mice
Sequencing method: Shotgun metagenomics (Ion Proton Sequencer)
Clinical characteristics measured: BMI, glucose, insulin, C-reactive protein, cholesterol
Study exclusion criteria: Antibiotic/antifungal use within 3 months, acute/chronic somatic disease
Regulatory approval: Regional Scientific Ethical Committee for Southern Denmark
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 age-matched female controls; Danish Caucasian women; AN-RS (n=56) and AN-BP (n=21)
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive study design and population information extracted from Methods and Results sections

host_species.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females; female germ-free Swiss Webster mice
host_species.notes: Study included both human participants (females) and laboratory mice (Mus musculus)

extraction_warnings: Sample-level granularity is partial: the paper reports aggregate statistics for n=77 AN cases and n=70 HC controls but does not provide individual participant identifiers or per-sample metadata tables. Six representative samples have been instantiated based on the FMT donor cohort (3 AN, 3 HC) to illustrate the study structure; the full human cohort contains 147 participants.
Age values not specified numerically in the main paper for most participants; only FMT donor ages (20, 22, 20 yr for AN; 20, 22, 21 yr for HC) are provided explicitly.
No individual NCBI accession numbers are reported in the provided text; accessions may be available in supplementary metadata or BioProject records not included here.

Serum samples were also collected and analyzed (metabolomics) but are not captured in the sample_id field since the schema is microbiome-focused and body_site is limited to predefined enum values; serum is not included.
The paper reports both human and mouse samples; the samples[] array instantiates human donor/recipient samples only, as the schema does not distinguish species.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Batch 1 subgroups ['AN (Anorexia Nervosa)', 'HC (Healthy Controls)', 'AN-RS (Anorexia Nervosa Restricting Subtype)', 'AN-BP (Anorexia Nervosa Binge-Purging Subtype)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Age range (13–53 years) inferred from EDI-3 questionnaire design rather than explicit study enrollment criteria; mean/median ages not reported for the full cohort of 77 AN and 70 HC participants.
BMI values reported only for 6 donors (3 AN-RS, 3 HC) used in FMT animal experiments, not for the full human cohort.
Smoking status used as covariate in analyses but prevalence/distribution not reported in main text or supplementary tables.
Medication use (SSRIs, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines) documented in Supplementary Table 2 but summary counts/prevalence not reported in main text.
Dietary restriction is central to AN pathophysiology but specific dietary intake details (calorie targets, specific foods avoided) not systematically reported for human participants.
Study noted as limited by lack of information on diet and physical activity—behaviors that impact gut microbiota.
The paper is observational and mechanistic; granularity is subgroup_level (AN, HC, AN-RS, AN-BP) not sample_level, as no per-participant metadata tables are provided.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
The schema fields were designed for oncology/clinical trial data but this paper is a mechanistic microbiota study with no tumor, survival, or ECOG status data
Biomarker values are mostly qualitative comparisons (higher/lower/enriched/depleted) rather than absolute numerical values
Feces_phenotype_value field repurposed to capture microbiota composition and functional changes in fecal samples
Paper focuses on associations and mechanistic relationships rather than discrete biomarker measurements with numerical values
